# Nebius raises Nvidia GPU rental rates up to 21% effective October 1, led by B300 at $9.50/hr

By Neil Rubin, with AI assistance

Published Sep 26, 8:00 PM EDT · Updated Oct 1, 12:08 PM EDT

- AI Monetization Bullish+1 sig 3

Why it matters

A supplier raising prices into record capex is the strongest possible signal that AI compute demand still exceeds supply — including for last-gen H100s, up 53% since May. It is bullish for the entire AI infrastructure revenue chain (Nvidia's pricing power, Micron's memory pricing power, datacenter landlords), and it is pure pricing power for neoclouds. The bearish offset is real: it raises the cost floor for AI startups' unit economics, which is exactly why falling inference costs matter to the thesis — someone has to make the math work for the renters. For the overbuild debate, this is bear-case kryptonite in price form: overbuilt markets cut prices; this market raises them.

## Summary Nebius raised on-demand AI compute pricing 17-21% across H100/H200/B200/B300 effective October 1, with the B300 going from $7.85 to $9.50/hour — into a year when it is spending $20-25B in capex on $3-3.4B guided revenue.

# Nebius verhoogt tarieven voor AI-rekenkracht met ruim 20 procent 

 Het verhuren van AI-rekenkracht in Europa wordt duurder. De in Nederland gevestigde AI-infrastructuuraanbieder Nebius verhoogt per 1 oktober 2026 de uurprijzen voor het huren van GPU's met 17 tot 21 procent. Dit blijkt uit de nieuwste Europese GPU-prijsindex van het onafhankelijke AI-onderzoeksbureau Lindstead. 

 

Door de prijsherziening stijgt het tarief voor een Nvidia H100 bij Nebius van circa 3,38 euro naar 3,95 euro per uur. De nieuwste generatie chips, de B300, gaat in prijs omhoog van ongeveer 6,88 euro naar 8,33 euro per uur. De prijsstijging past binnen een bredere ontwikkeling in de markt: de mediane huurprijs van een H200-GPU steeg in een jaar tijd met ongeveer 25 procent, waarbij elke nieuwe chipgeneratie duurder is per uur dan de voorgaande.

## Goedkoper dan bij Amerikaanse hyperscalers

Ondanks de prijsverhoging blijven Europese aanbieders aanzienlijk goedkoper dan de grote Amerikaanse hyperscalers. Uit de Lindstead-index blijkt dat het huren van een H100 bij Europese partijen zoals het Franse OVHcloud (circa 2,62 euro per uur), het Finse Verda (3,09 euro per uur) en Nebius ongeveer de helft kost van vergelijkbare capaciteit bij AWS en Microsoft Azure, en circa een derde van het tarief bij Google Cloud.

Naast de prijs speelt data-soevereiniteit een steeds grotere rol bij de keuzes van Europese organisaties. Lindstead wijst erop dat Amerikaanse cloudproviders onder de US CLOUD Act vallen, zelfs als hun datacenters fysiek op Europees grondgebied staan. Voor organisaties die werken met privacygevoelige gegevens zijn de eigendomsverhoudingen en het geldende rechtstelsel doorslaggevend. De lagere tarieven van Europese leveranciers maken de overstap naar regionale infrastructuur voor veel bedrijven financieel en strategisch aantrekkelijk.

# On 1 October 2026, Nebius raises its on-demand GPU prices by 17 to 21 percent. | Lindstead · LinkedIn · 2026-09-28T00:00:00+00:00

**Lindstead**.

---

On 1 October 2026, Nebius raises its on-demand GPU prices by 17 to 21 percent.

Nebius is headquartered in Amsterdam and listed on Nasdaq. Its list prices per GPU-hour change as follows:
• H100: €3.38 to €3.95
• H200: €3.95 to €4.74
• B200: €6.27 to €7.45
• B300: €6.88 to €8.33

It fits a wider pattern:
• The median rental price of an H200 rose by about 25 percent in twelve months.
• Each newer GPU generation costs more per hour.

For organisations planning to run AI on infrastructure they control, the cost side of the business case is moving. Committed-use discounts of up to 35 percent are available at several providers, so contract terms now matter as much as list prices.

results.title: Nebius just confirmed the price increase we flagged as unconfirmed last week. Its live now. | Devanshu Rajput
results.author: Devanshu Rajput
highlights:
**Devanshu Rajput**: Growth & Marketing Intern @ ComputeStacker | Content Marketing | SEO | Market Research | Social Media | AI & Technology.

---

Nebius just confirmed the price increase we flagged as unconfirmed last week. Its live now.

H100 pricing on Nebius went from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU-hour, confirmed directly against their own pricing page, a 17% increase. H200 rose 20%, from $4.50 to $5.40. B300 climbed 21%, reaching $9.50. This is Nebius's second rate hike since May, when H100 was still priced at $2.95.

According to GetDeploying's pricing tracker, the median on-demand H100 across 40 providers sat at $3.42/GPU-hour as of September 28, up 15% year over year. The same tracker puts hyperscaler pricing at roughly 58% above specialized GPU clouds for the same chip.

Nobody builds a futures market for a commodity that's reliably getting cheaper. CME Group is launching GPU rental price futures on October 5. That alone signals where this market expects prices to go next.

If a provider quoted you a GPU rate more than a few weeks ago, it's worth checking that number again before you plan a budget around it.

highlights:
# Chmura AI drożeje 

 Nebius poinformował klientów o podniesieniu stawek za wynajem mocy obliczeniowej GPU od 1 października. 

 Publikacja: 28.09.2026 06:00 

 Konrad Ogrodowicz, zarządzający funduszami, Superfund TFI 

 Foto: materiały prasowe 

 Konrad Ogrodowicz 

 To już druga podwyżka w ciągu trzech miesięcy. Instancje z chipami Nvidia H100 zdrożeją o ok. 17 proc., H200 o 20 proc., B200 o ok. 19 proc., a najnowsze B300 najmocniej, bo o 21 proc. Stawka za godzinę pracy H100 wzrośnie z 3,85 do 4,50 USD, a za H200 z 4,50 do 5,40 USD. Drożeją także CPU i pamięć. Stawki za część usług opartych na procesorach AMD EPYC Genoa rosną o ok. 25 proc., a za pamięć o ok. 41 proc., co jest największą podwyżką w nowym cenniku. 

 Wielu inwestorów obawia się, że zbliżamy się do szczytu cyklu AI, a tym samym do szczytu notowań spółek technologicznych. Na razie ta teza nie znajduje jednak potwierdzenia w danych napływających z rynku. Popyt na moc obliczeniową jest tak duży, że każda nowa moc jest w pełni wykorzystywana. Do tego branża napotyka kolejne wąskie gardła, które spowalniają inwestycje. Ostatnio głośno było o problemach z przyłączami energetycznymi w Teksasie, gdzie kolejka oczekujących na podłączenie do sieci jest zbyt długa. 

 Inwestorzy przyjęli podwyżki pozytywnie, a akcje Nebiusa zyskały ok. 8 proc. W mojej ocenie neochmury to jedna z ciekawszych inwestycji na najbliższy rok. Czołówkę tego sektora tworzą Nebius, CoreWeave i IREN. Oczekiwania inwestorów są wysokie, ale, jak widać, wciąż jest sporo miejsca na pozytywne zaskoczenia. Spółki te są dopiero na początku drogi, a jednocześnie dysponują potężnym portfelem zamówień, którego rynek, moim zdaniem, jeszcze w pełni nie wycenił.

results.title: Amazon hiking AI chip rental prices, exploring Nvidia leaseback
results.author: Cris Tolomia
highlights:
Amazon announced a roughly 15% price increase on its EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML service, which lets customers reserve access to Nvidia chips ranging from the older A100 to the newer B300, with updated rates taking effect next week, according to MarketWatch. 

Separately, Amazon has approached outside investors about a deal that would transfer roughly $8 billion in Nvidia Grace Blackwell chips into a special-purpose vehicle and then lease those chips back, according to the Financial Times, as cited by Reuters. Under the arrangement, the SPV would be funded through debt sold to outside investors, and Amazon would hold an equity interest of as much as 10% in the vehicle, the Financial Times reported. Amazon either purchased or leased the chips in question, which are already operating at facilities spread across five U.S. states — among them Nevada and Virginia — at more than a dozen sites in total. 

The pricing page notes that current rates are scheduled to be updated next in October 2026. EC2 Capacity Block pricing consists of an upfront reservation fee plus an operating system fee, the company said. For example, the p5.48xlarge instance — which runs eight Nvidia H100 chips — is listed at $41.528 per hour in major U.S. regions. 

The two moves together reflect the pressure Amazon faces in financing its AI infrastructure expansion. The proposed sale-leaseback structure would let Amazon lighten its balance sheet by transferring the financial burden of costly chips to third-party investors, according to the Financial Times.

results.title: GPU rental prices are going up, not down. | Peter Lee
results.author: Peter Lee
highlights:
---

GPU rental prices are going up, not down.

Nebius raises rates October 1 — its second hike in three months:
• H100: +17%
• H200: +20%
• B200: +19%
• B300: +21%

Wall Street just split wide open on what it means. JPMorgan upgraded CoreWeave to Overweight ($125 target): pricing power, not debt, is the story — short-term compute now sells at a steep premium, some rivals at ~3x long-term rates.

Days earlier, Rothschild & Co Redburn initiated both CoreWeave and Nebius at Sell, calling neocloud earnings "cyclically inflated."
Both can't be right about durability. But both agree on the present: compute is a seller's market.

Behind the curtain, input costs keep climbing. Mainstream DDR4 closed at $46.11 on Sept 24 (TrendForce) — roughly 4x late-2025 levels — and HBM is effectively sold out for 2026. Memory, not GPUs, is the binding constraint on new capacity.

If you buy compute: review your rate card before Q4 renewals. The "GPU prices only fall" assumption is broken for now — and long-dated fixed-price contracts just flipped from hedge to liability.
Is this pricing power durable, or cyclical?

In October 2026, EU-headquartered cloud providers list an NVIDIA H100 at €2.80 to €3.95 per GPU hour on demand. The US hyperscalers charge €6.03 (AWS), €6.12 (Azure) and €9.70 (Google Cloud). Nebius raised its on-demand GPU prices on 1 October 2026. All figures are published list prices, accessed 1 October 2026, with the source per row.

1. EU-headquartered providers rent an H100 for €2.80 to €3.95 an hour, about half the AWS and Azure price.

results.title: Nvidia B200 Price Hits $8.01/Hr as GPU Costs Diverge
results.author: Tom Vance
highlights:
Tom Vance Updated Oct 25, 2026 · 15 min read

Renting a Nvidia B200 by the hour has no single market price, because Nvidia does not sell it by the GPU-hour and each cloud sets its own rate. Listings in November 2026 reportedly run from $4.11 per GPU-hour, the lowest listed on-demand rate, at Beam Cloud to $16.11 per GPU-hour. Google Cloud listed $16.11 on demand in us-west1 on November 6. Treat any single average, including one quoted from the SemiAnalysis GPU pricing index, as a snapshot to check against provider pages. The B200 is listed as available for rental across multiple cloud providers as of November 6, 2026, and its status is active. It is no longer the only Blackwell option: HGX B300 systems based on Blackwell Ultra became generally available on Google Distributed Cloud air-gapped deployments on October 20, 2026, and Vera Rubin NVL72 is marked early access. Older B200 snapshots, H100 and H200 prices, and any one provider’s rate should not be read as the current market-wide B200 price. Check each provider’s current terms before you commit.

...

## Nvidia B200 Cloud Rental Prices Jump 79% in Three Months

The core data point comes from the SemiAnalysis GPU pricing index, which tracks day-to-day cloud rental rates across a basket of providers. In late September 2026, that index put B200 rental pricing at $8.01 per GPU-hour, a 79% climb from where it sat three months earlier. That figure is a market average rather than a price Nvidia publishes or any single provider charges, and a separate October 2026 report from Uvik put B200 median rental pricing at $8.19/GPU-hour across 9 providers, a similar level measured a different way. The same analysis calculated that a B200 now costs 21% more per unit of compute than an H100, a full reversal from June 2026, when a B200 was actually 18% cheaper than an H100 on the same compute-adjusted basis.

...

None of this happens in a vacuum. High-bandwidth memory production is concentrated among a small number of suppliers, and 2026 has been a year of persistent HBM tightness across the entire AI hardware stack. Nvidia’s own next-generation Rubin Ultra platform has reportedly had to trim memory allocation per package because of the same shortage, and cloud providers including Nebius have already raised prices to reflect higher input costs on memory-heavy configurations. When the memory that feeds B200 and H200 packages is scarce and expensive to source, that cost gets passed straight through to the hourly rental rate. Nvidia itself has acknowledged the squeeze: on October 21, 2026, it announced plans with supply-chain partners to expand manufacturing capacity for AI infrastructure, citing extraordinary demand and constrained capacity.

...

### How B200 Rental Prices Differ by Provider and Billing Type

The $8.01 index figure is an average, so the price a team actually pays depends on the provider and on how the capacity is billed. In October 2026, Cloud-GPUs tracked B200 availability across 14 providers in 27 countries and listed B200 spot rates at $3.95 to $8.75/GPU-hour, while GPU Economy listed Google Cloud’s B200 spot rate at $1.45/hour. In November 2026, Modal listed B200 at $6.25/GPU-hour, Lambda listed an 8×B200 instance at $6.69/GPU-hour, and Runpod Secure Cloud listed B200 at $7.99/GPU-hour.

Older listings show how wide the spread already was. In February 2025, GPUTracker listed B200 spot pricing at $1.67/hour from Verda. In February 2025, GPUTracker listed B200 on-demand pricing at $3.40/hour from Vast.ai, and it listed Lambda’s B200 on-demand price at $3.99/hour. It also listed GB200 on-demand pricing at $6.50/hour from CoreWeave in February 2025.

Put together, these listings mean that spot, on-demand and whole-instance prices are different products, and a single headline rate hides that. An eight-GPU hyperscaler instance and a single-GPU marketplace listing are not interchangeable, so a budget built on the index average can be wrong in either direction. Before committing to a provider, compare like with like: the same billing model, the same GPU count per instance and the same date. Historical rates should be treated as history rather than as a quote, and a spot price should not be assumed to stay available for a long-running job.

...

Cloud providers themselves are caught in the middle. Neoclouds like CoreWeave, which made HGX B200 instances generally available in May 2025, and Lambda Labs, which built businesses around reselling Nvidia capacity, have to pass through higher acquisition costs or eat margin. Some have already chosen the former: Nebius, one of the higher-profile AI-cloud operators, raised its own pricing in 2026 citing rising memory costs, and it reportedly lifted its B200 on-demand rate from $7.15 to $8.50 per GPU-hour on October 1, 2026, a move and a price level that line up directly with the HBM scarcity driving the B200 and H200 numbers here.
